statement: Hiyu Wine Farm is based in Hood River, Oregon, and the producer's current site lists 3890 Acree Drive, Hood River.
Nate Ready and China Tresemer are documented co-founders of Hiyu Wine Farm; Ready is the winemaker and Tresemer is closely associated with the farm and its agricultural work.

Hiyu distinguishes Hiyu wines, which come from named fields on the home farm, from Tzum wines, which come from small specific fields throughout the Columbia Gorge; importer material likewise describes Tzum as site-specific wines from nearby leased plots.
Moon Hill Farm is a two-acre vineyard adjacent to Hiyu; the sites were once part of the same farm, Hiyu has cared for Moon Hill since 2015, and the parcel is held under a long-term lease.
scope_notes: This records farming and observed tenure language, not ownership; the source does not establish the lease’s exact start or end.
CARTA does not equate the Wente selection with Dijon clone 96 and does not infer a more precise clonal genealogy than the source states.
statement: Moon Hill Farm was planted in 2010 to Chardonnay, including an heirloom California Wente selection and cuttings from Celilo Vineyard, with smaller amounts of Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir.
The Tzum Moon Hill Farm wine is documented as approximately 80% Chardonnay with the balance Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir.

scope_notes: This is temporal production history attached to one durable wine identity, not a basis for vintage-specific wine entities.
statement: The Moon Hill wine was assembled from wines of the same plot from the 2015 through 2020 vintages after separate vinification and aging; in spring 2021 the components were assembled in 500-liter puncheons with an intent to maintain a solera-like system.

scope_notes: The source supports restaurant work and an apprenticeship at Antica Terra; CARTA does not infer broader stylistic influence beyond that.
statement: Importer reporting describes Nate Ready as a former sommelier at high-end California restaurants including The French Laundry and identifies an apprenticeship with Maggie Harrison at Antica Terra as especially important in his development.
The Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau recognizes Columbia Gorge as an American Viticultural Area.

scope_notes: This records producer-specific farming descriptions and does not create a certification claim.
statement: Current producer and importer materials describe Hiyu as an integrated mixed farm using organic and regenerative approaches, dry farming, agroforestry, and animal integration around the vineyard landscape.

scope_notes: Individual Hiyu and Tzum wines can differ materially in pressing, maceration, vessel, and élevage; this claim records recurring practices rather than a fixed recipe.
statement: Hiyu's current materials document hand work, wild fermentation, whole-cluster handling in parts of the range, neutral-wood use, and long maturation, with technique varying by field and wine.
Domaine Christiane Chambeyron-Manin is a micro-estate in Côte-Rôtie currently owned and run by Véronique Manin.

scope_notes: CARTA does not extend this source into unsupported genealogy involving other Chambeyron or Levet domaines.
statement: The Wine Trust identifies Christiane as Véronique Manin's mother and explains that the domaine name incorporates family names from Véronique's maternal and paternal lines.
The domaine farms a single roughly 0.5-hectare parcel on Côte Brune above Ampuis; importer descriptions place it on iron-rich schist with a very steep slope and hand-worked vines.

scope_notes: The accepted evidence supports organic-method farming language, not formal organic certification.
statement: The Wine Trust describes Chambeyron-Manin's vineyard work as sustainable and using organic methods; CARTA does not treat this as evidence of formal certification.

Chambeyron-Manin's Côte-Rôtie is made from Syrah from the domaine's 0.5-hectare Côte Brune parcel; importer sources describe the parcel as planted exclusively to Syrah using the local 'Sérine' selection/clone terminology.

Sacred Thirst describes the Chambeyron-Manin parcel as dedicated to the 'Serine clone of syrah.' CARTA treats Sérine here as local selection/clone terminology attached to Syrah, not as a separate grape identity or a universal synonym claim.

scope_notes: CARTA rejects the stronger claim that the wine is aged in concrete; the more detailed source distinguishes concrete fermentation from oak élevage.
statement: Sacred Thirst documents whole-cluster native-yeast fermentation in concrete tanks, basket pressing, transfer by gravity into 500-liter barrels with up to one-third new oak depending on vintage, and about 18 months of élevage before unfined, unfiltered bottling.

scope_notes: No pre-phylloxera or own-rooted status is asserted.
statement: Current importer material describes the Syrah vines as roughly 40 to more than 50 years old.
INAO recognizes Côte-Rôtie as an AOC and provides the current homologated specification through its official product page.
Trade reporting describes Goyo García Viadero as coming from a Ribera del Duero winemaking family and setting out independently in 2003, while also making wines in Cantabria.

Beâtum is the Liébana label/project within Goyo García Viadero's work, represented by Beâtum Blanco and Beâtum Tinto; CARTA keeps it distinct from the producer identity rather than treating it as a separate estate.

José Pastor Selections documents Beâtum Blanco as 100% old bush-vine Palomino grown on brown slate between roughly 500 and 600 meters around Potes in the Valle de Liébana, fermented on skins in stainless steel without added yeast, sulfur, or other exogenous winemaking products.

scope_notes: Blend percentages can vary by vintage or source; this claim reflects the documented importer reference and does not define a timeless formula.
statement: José Pastor Selections documents Beâtum Tinto as approximately 80% Mencía and 20% Palomino from at least 80-year-old vines on broken slate, co-fermented with wild yeasts in steel and raised for 12 months in old French oak without added SO2.
The 2009 official amendment for Vino de la Tierra de Liébana lists Palomino among authorized white varieties and Mencía among authorized red varieties.

The Government of Cantabria continues to maintain a registration procedure for growers, producers and bottlers using the Vino de la Tierra de Liébana designation and cites the 2005, 2006 and 2009 governing orders.
Importer documentation places the Beâtum wines around Potes in Valle de Liébana, Picos de Europa, Cantabria.
